A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TACO research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original completion, segmentation, reconstruction and pose-estimation experiments, a 36-participant user study, ablations and supplementary qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Diffusion-VAS comparisons and image-level evaluations on BSDS-A and Kubric-Img.

M1.justification: The SVD-based architecture, video and mask conditioning, progressive training and sliding-window inference remain unchanged. Repeating still images into videos in Appendix C.1 prepares inputs for the added evaluation; it does not revise TACO's algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds image-only evaluation: BSDS-A for amodal segmentation and Kubric-Img for completion and segmentation. Kubric-Img uses images from the existing Kubric-Static dataset but removes temporal context. All original training, video-evaluation and downstream-task coverage remains.

E2.justification: Diffusion-VAS, previously discussed only as related work, is added to the Kubric-Static and Kubric-Dynamic comparisons in Table 1 and Figure 4. The new BSDS-A table also includes a Modal-mask reference. Existing comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The new image evaluation repeats each image 14 times. BSDS-A uses 200 images containing 730 objects, one randomly selected annotation per image and single-shot inference for both methods. Kubric-Img uses 750 images with 30–70% occlusion. Previously reported evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 adds a targeted test of completion without neighboring-frame information using repeated still images. The progressive-training ablation, missing-object examples, long-video demonstrations, sampling-diversity examples and failure-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without adding seed information, repeated-experiment variability, confidence intervals or statistical tests. The new single-shot image setting specifies inference sampling, rather than an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results remain unchanged. Added Diffusion-VAS results alter Kubric rankings: its Static/Dynamic IoU is 84.3/77.8 versus TACO's 83.9/77.4, and CLIP-T is 0.971/0.977 versus 0.970/0.970. Tables S.6–S.7 add mixed image-level results, including BSDS-A IoU of 67.6 for TACO versus 68.9 for pix2gestalt.

T1.justification: The task formulation, diffusion equations, sliding-window equation and appendix occlusion-overlay formulas are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims about consistent video completion, scalable data curation, progressive training, generalization and downstream applications. The image-only findings are not promoted into new headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 now acknowledges Diffusion-VAS's segmentation advantage and suggests its explicit mask prediction explains it. Appendix C.1 attributes image-only performance to persistent-occlusion training and qualifies comparisons with published pix2gestalt results because annotation selection and sampling differ. Existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 documents how to construct static-video inputs and select annotations and images for the added evaluations, including the unavailability of pix2gestalt's exact annotation choices. Existing training epochs, hardware, batch sizes, resolutions, sampler settings and project URL remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for the BSDS source, Coarse-to-fine amodal segmentation with shape prior, Trace3D and three embodied or 3D vision-language works. Diffusion-VAS was already cited in v1 but now becomes an evaluated competitor. The broader related-work positioning is retained; several other references only receive publication updates.

P1.justification: There are limited edits to the abstract, introduction, results discussion and appendix prose, plus a new acknowledgment. Inserting Appendix C.1 shifts the existing C subsections, while the main section organization and most wording remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains Diffusion-VAS rows and revised best-score highlighting; Figure 4 gains a D-VAS column. Tables S.6–S.7 and Figure S.19 are new. Some figures are resized and material reflows, while the remaining appendix images are retained after renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical coverage through a directly relevant video-amodal competitor and image-only tests, while acknowledging the competitor's segmentation advantage. These are useful, limited gains. The explanation linking image-only success to persistent-occlusion training is not isolated experimentally, and Table 1's retained caption now overstates superiority in mask alignment and consistency.
